safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not state that there were no previous similar episodes.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether this is a first-ever episode versus recurrent similar episodes affects risk stratification (e.g., new/unstable angina vs chronic stable symptoms) and the urgency/diagnostic framing. Omission may reduce clarity of the clinical narrative but is unlikely to change the immediate disposition here (ambulance/ED evaluation).

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated contains no statement of haemodynamic stability.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting haemodynamic stability is important in suspected ACS because instability would escalate urgency and immediate management (e.g., resuscitation-level response). If omitted, downstream clinicians may lack a key triage datapoint, though EMS/ED will reassess vitals on arrival.

safety_verdicts.content: Urgent ECG and troponin T are required.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes ECG but does not mention troponin T requirement.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In suspected acute coronary syndrome, troponin testing is a core diagnostic step; omitting it from the stated urgent plan could contribute to incomplete handover or delayed recognition of required investigations. Although the ED will typically order troponins routinely, this omission can still pose meaningful risk of delay or miscommunication.

This can adversely affect safety and treatment choices even if EMS/ED later reconciles meds.
